<meta>continues from previous page: ...to which they added a third part of quicksilver, so that the water might be coagulated. Afterward, they sublimated the mercury so many times with the aforementioned vitriol and sal ammoniac; thus, it came to pass that it</meta> carried itself forward. Indeed, arsenic can certainly not be fixed at all unless the artist, the operator, has an equal knowledge of its coloring spirit, regarding which all philosophers have slumbered, attempting in vain to produce anything from it. Whoever, therefore, is ignorant of this spirit should have no hope of fixing it, nor of attributing to it that power by which it might acquire the perfection of transmutation. For this reason, I make it known to all that the whitening about which mention has been made is taken from a false foundation, and that by it, copper is falsely whitened, not transmuted. The <term>sophistae</term> <gloss>sophists/pseudo-alchemists</gloss>, having masked and painted Venus <note>the alchemical term for copper</note> in this manner, mixed it with double its weight of moon <note>the alchemical term for silver</note>, and sold it to goldsmiths and moneyers. Ultimately, however, they transformed themselves into counterfeiters, not only those who sold it, but also those who bought it. Some of the sophists took red arsenic instead of white, and this itself resulted in a false art; for, in whatever way it may be prepared, it exhibits nothing but whiteness. Some have gone further, to common sulfur, which they cooked with vinegar, lye, or very sharp urines, day and night, until it emerged white. Afterward, they lifted it from common salt and eggshell through sublimation and cooked it, and sublimated it, and did so many times; nevertheless, it remained always combustible, even though it was white. Yet, to fix the crude mercury by this means...

<summary>Paracelsus condemns the failed and deceptive methods used by "sophists" to whiten copper or manipulate arsenic and sulfur, asserting that these techniques fail to achieve true transmutation because they ignore the underlying chemical nature of the spirits involved.</summary>
<keywords>arsenic, Sophists, transmutation, whitening, Venus, copper, moon, silver, mercury, sulfur, fixation</keywords>
